translation:
Without fever but fearing cold, it issues from yin; instead it does not summon the formation of a glomus-pi (stuffing) fullness. Press it and it does not pain — cold damage of blood; chest and diaphragm fullness distinguish descending and no ascent.
Fever with aversion to cold issues from yang; wrongly purging opens the door and injures the thief. Press and then it pains: binding in the chest, small (結胸小); unoppressed it pains by itself: large, grievous to bear.
Heat binding in the chest is vexed and thirsty; cold binding in the chest is oppressed and fears coolness. Water binding in the chest is swollen and sweats; do not lightly and wrongly purge, consult otherwise apart.
translator_notes: The verse plays on 結胸小/大 (small vs large chest binding).
unresolved: "結胸小" could be "結胸下", 結胸 by descent
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）

translation:
The spleen is the central center wu-ji earth; in diseases of the Great Yin (Taiyin) the abdomen bears suffering. Yang toxin invading as pathogen, the hands and feet are warm; pain has stoppages, and speech is profuse.
Fullness without the least growth — so it stops there; yin toxin giving rise is different again. Abdominal fullness desiring defecation without rest; fullness together with accumulated blood stasis can be dispersed and distinguished.
translator_notes: "滿無稍長"= fullness with no gradual growth.
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）

translation:
Cold pathogen injuring the middle strikes the three yang of the foot; the interstices being firmly closed, it wreaks havoc outside. Fluids seep internally without sweat-rain; Mahuang Tang (Ephedra Decoction) to release the exterior is best.
Cold pathogen injuring the middle strikes the three yin of the foot; the interstices being loose, sweat drips by itself. Flowing without stop is a yang-collapse condition; in Guizhi Tang (Cinnamon Twig Decoction) inside one may search.
Thief-sweat (daohan) steals and flows within dreams; on waking it ceases, leaving no trace of its shadow. Half exterior and half interior, the pathogen coils and squats; gallbladder-heat, Chaihu Tang (Bupleurum Decoction) one cup.
When the pathogen fights at the boundary of the various yang, naturally the head sweats down to the neck and returns. Prolonged rain without clearing is yang collapse; Huangqi Tang combined with Guizhi (Cinnamon Twig) is gathered.
Hands and feet are the branches and leaves of the spleen and stomach; cold transforms from fire in the central region. Fluids pour in profusion, sweating from the four limbs; Qingpí Yin (Clear the Spleen Beverage) taken, the effect is swift.
translator_notes: 麻黃湯=Mahuang Tang; 桂枝湯=Guizhi Tang; 黃耆湯=Huangqi Tang; 清脾飲=Qingpí Yin.
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）
